necessary_outcome_disposition.reason: Necessary outcome dependency after new source-specific original review resolves2318toFiske2015, not the old Smabyassay citation. New MSA observations compare token-versus-primary efficacy directly toFiske2015and the authors conclude their results support and extend that study. Similar efficacy for some learners and variation across others reproduce the original individually variable efficacy finding; consistency for Annie/Jack is not an author-declared failure. The no-backup-token component is the weakest reinforcement condition for every current learner, supporting the substantive backup-availability comparison. Preserve the internal reporting tension: Discussion broadly says responding was at/below EXT, but actual Annie/Jack means exceed the stated EXTmeans; do not claim all participant comparisons agree numerically. The authors central empirical synthesis still supports the original target. The change from PRbreakpoints to MSAresponse rates does not itself exclude conceptual replication. Source reports new observations, not reuse of2015data, but full participant-level nonoverlap is not asserted. Earlier descriptive-only verdict applied to a different, method-supplying original and cannot be transferred to the now-resolved empirical target.
